results.title: Why I Built a 4.1 MB Native macOS Screen Recorder in Swift Instead of Using Electron - DEV Community
results.content:
I record product demos and coding walkthroughs on my Mac almost every day, and I kept running into the same annoying trade-off:

- macOS built-in capture (`⌘⇧5`) is instant and lightweight, but has zero live teaching tools — no screen pen, no zoom magnifier, no teleprompter.
- Heavy studio recorders bundle hundreds of megabytes, spin up the fans, lock basic workflows behind monthly subscriptions, and force you to sit through slow re-encoding exports after every short recording.

So I built LeanTake in pure Swift, AppKit, and Apple's `ScreenCaptureKit` — a 4.1 MB notarized macOS app focused on finishing every demo in a single take.

Website & Free DMG: 

## Key Engineering Choices

### 1. Real-Time Hardware Encoding = Zero Export Wait [...] ### 1. Real-Time Hardware Encoding = Zero Export Wait

Instead of writing raw intermediate frames and forcing a post-production render queue, LeanTake hardware-encodes directly to `.mov` in real time. The instant you press Stop (`⌃⌥R`), the finished file is ready to play or share in Finder.

### 2. Live 12-Color Pen & Region Magnifier

While explaining code or tiny UI controls, you can trigger a live pen (pencil, lines, arrows, shapes, eraser) or region magnifier on a shortcut — and hit `Esc` to clear every stroke and return immediately to normal mouse clicks.

### 3. 9 3D Cat Paw & Glove Cursors (Video-Only) [...] I dislike forced logins for local desktop utilities. The core recorder (720p/1080p, no watermark, unlimited recording time, pencil, magnifier, Cotton Glove) is free forever. Optional Pro is a $14.99 one-time lifetime license for up to 3 Macs verified locally via Ed25519 signed tokens.

Requirements: macOS 15.0+ on Apple Silicon.

Would love feedback from fellow Swift / macOS builders — what shortcuts or workflow tweaks do you rely on most when recording technical demos?

## 3. Ensure Hardware Encoding Is Active

Ensure your recording software is configured to use hardware-accelerated encoding (such as Apple hardware encoding or GPU encoding) instead of software encoding (CPU), which is slow and drops frames.

## 4. Run the Recorder Natively (Bypass Web Wrappers)

Many popular screen recording tools are built on web tech frameworks like Electron. These apps run a complete browser instance in the background, consuming large amounts of memory. Switching to a native Mac recorder can instantly resolve lag issues.

Founder of ScreenKite. Mike records product demos and lessons on a Mac, and builds the recorder and editor he wanted for that work. [...] The Native Fix: ScreenKite is built natively on macOS. It skips Electron overhead and records smoothly at 60 FPS. Download ScreenKite for Mac →

## 1. Close CPU and GPU-Heavy Applications

Screen recording requires substantial processing power. If you are running complex IDEs, video editors, or multiple browser tabs, they compete for the same hardware resources:

- Open Activity Monitor and check the CPU and Memory tabs.
- Close any applications using high percentages of resources before starting your recording.

## 2. Scale Down Your Display Resolution

results.title: The best screen recording software for Mac I tested for work and content creation
results.content:
### My go-to screen recorder for Mac

Finding the perfect screen recorder for my work isn’t easy. Recording is only one part of the process. Once you’re done, you need to trim, annotate, or lightly edit the video before you share it.

Being someone who’s not really adept at video editing, I need a screen recorder that’s easy to use. No complicated navigation, and definitely free of confusing jargon.

In no particular order, these are the best screen recorders I found.

### Mac’s native screen recorder

Press enter or click to view image in full size

Image 5

Mac’s native screen recorder is a dependable option — particularly if you’re concerned about performance lag when recording. It lets you record the entire screen or a specific area.

What I like [...] What I like

Because it’s built into macOS, you don’t need to download it separately. Just press Shift + Command + 5, and you’ll be able to record right away.

What I didn’t like

The tool is very limited. I couldn’t capture the camera feed. And if I wanted to edit the clip, I’d have to use another tool like QuickTime Player.

### Cleanshot X

Image 6

For the best screen recorder for Mac, I’d say that Cleanshot X wins hands down. Cleanshot X lets you record both video and GIFs with an easy-to-use interface.

Unlike Mac’s native screen recorder, Cleanshot X supports mic and camera recording. I’ve tried it, and I sounded and looked sharp in the recorded clip.
